content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee: Edward Fleming (E042), requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory has two notes:
- Note 1 says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Comment says full-time may have up to write; write is within policy. Recommend write.
- Note 2 says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Comment says Security DB is authoritative, contractor with basic training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.

So there's a conflict: full_time vs contractor. Security note says Security DB is authoritative. The employee is a contractor with basic security training.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

The Security DB is authoritative per note 2, so treat as contractor. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
